source_video.title_hint: Surrounded: Glenn Greenwald vs 20 Trump Supporters

move: Open each round by extracting the challenger's own definition, then lock the debate to it
how_it_works: He asks 'what makes a peacemaking president?', gets the challenger to volunteer 'prevention,' then holds them to their own criteria so every later answer is judged against a standard they authored.
evidence_quote: so first, I want to just ask, what makes a peacemaking president? ... so you agree that prevention is a part of what makes a president a peacemaking president. For sure.
counter: Refuse to give a clean one-line definition first; counter-define the proposition's key term yourself before answering, forcing him to argue your frame.
effectiveness: won — the challenger spends the rest of the round trapped defending against his own conceded definition
confidence: high — explicit definitional setup at lines 49-62

move: Counter the 'he ended the war so he's a peacemaker' defense with a self-inflicted-wound analogy
how_it_works: Accepts the premise (he ended it) but reframes: ending a war you yourself started is not peacemaking. The stab-then-ER image makes the logic vivid and audience-sticky.
evidence_quote: It's like saying, I stabbed myself in the stomach, but then I brought myself to the ER where I had a doctor fix me up, and that proves that I'm really interested in fitness and self-care.
counter: Deny he 'started' it — establish a prior state of conflict so there is no clean baseline of peace to have broken.
effectiveness: won — challenger cannot dislodge the analogy and pivots to justifying the war instead

move: Name the opponent's slogan as Orwellian 'war is peace' propaganda
how_it_works: When the challenger argues you prevent conflicts by engaging in conflicts, Greenwald compresses it to 'so war is peace' and tags it to 1984, converting their position into a self-discrediting label.
evidence_quote: So war is peace. Did you read 1984 by George Orwell? ... one of the things citizens get told is war is peace.
counter: Reject the compression: distinguish deterrence/prevention from Orwellian doublespeak before he can attach the label.
effectiveness: won — challenger is reduced to 'you can't prevent conflicts by starting conflicts' on Greenwald's terms

move: Force a binary yes/no ('Were we at war with Iran when Trump took office?') and refuse to let go
how_it_works: He repeatedly demands a one-word answer to a question whose honest answer ('no') concedes his proposition, treating every evasive elaboration as confirmation he must keep pressing.
evidence_quote: Were we at war with Iran when President Trump was inaugurated? ... Are we at war now? ... So he made that war, right? He was a war maker.
counter: Refuse the false binary openly: 'War and conflict aren't a clean on/off switch — and here's why the date you picked is arbitrary,' then redefine the timeline.
effectiveness: won — the challenger keeps saying 'it depends how you define war,' which the audience reads as dodging

move: The challenger's 'it depends how you're defining war' dodge to avoid conceding the war started under Trump
how_it_works: Faced with a binary that concedes the point either way, he retreats into definitional ambiguity ('conflict' vs 'war' vs 'operation') to deny a fixed start date.
evidence_quote: It depends on how you're defining war. It depends on how you're defining war and long-term conflict.
counter: Greenwald's actual counter: pin them to their OWN earlier answer ('As you said the first time when I asked you, with Iran, when President Trump took office') so the redefinition reads as contradiction.
effectiveness: lost — the dodge is visible; Greenwald catches the contradiction and the challenger gets voted out

move: Turn the opponent's own proxy-definition against them: 'you can't define war one way for Trump and another for Biden'
how_it_works: The challenger defined Trump's Yemen action as a war via proxies, then refused to call Biden's proxy-funding a war on Iran. Greenwald flags the asymmetric standard to collapse their position.
evidence_quote: So you can't define war one way for Trump, and not... And you defined it by the proxies in Yemen.
counter: Apply one consistent definition from the outset; never let the standard for your side differ from the standard for the opponent's side.
effectiveness: won — exposes the double standard right before the buzzer

move: Pre-empt the opponent's 'one counterexample = not subservient' frame and label it before he builds it
how_it_works: When 'Nick Mattel' tries to redefine 'subservient' as requiring total obedience, Greenwald names the move ('you want to set it up so that if you can point to one example...') and offers to concede instances precisely to deny him the binary win.
evidence_quote: You wanna set it up so that if you can point to one example where President Trump didn't do what Israel wanted, then that means somehow he's not subservient to Israel.
counter: Don't telegraph the binary; instead make HIM define 'subservient' precisely first, then hold him to whether his evidence meets that bar.
effectiveness: neutral — Greenwald blocks the trap but the round bogs down in semantics over 'subservient'
confidence: medium — strong block, but the term-fight muddied the exchange (lines 707-735)

move: Extract the explicit 'who sets war goals?' admission, then trap on Trump's own 'free the Iranian people' quote
how_it_works: He walks the challenger to admit the President sets war goals, then asks whether Trump's stated goal of 'freeing the Iranian people' is regime change — forcing a yes that concedes Trump fights the regime-change wars he disavowed.
evidence_quote: Has Donald Trump said that a goal of the war in Iran is to free the Iranian people by changing the regime ... Did Donald Trump say that was a goal of the war or not? ... He said it in interviews. Yes. Thank you.
counter: Distinguish 'positive externality' from 'war aim' EARLY (as a later challenger did at line 2296) instead of conceding the quote after being cornered.
effectiveness: won — drags out a one-word 'Yes' that concedes the proposition

move: Counter the 'America votes with its dollar' defense of AIPAC by flipping it into a deception charge
how_it_works: Challenger 'Eden' argues AIPAC succeeds because Americans want it. Greenwald accepts the premise then redirects: AIPAC hides the Israel issue and runs on potholes/healthcare precisely because Americans DON'T care about it — so the spending proves the opposite.
evidence_quote: They don't go in and advertise and say, this member of Congress isn't supportive of Israel ... What they do is they go in and they deceive people by saying, our ads are really about ... potholes
counter: Concede the ad-targeting but argue it's ordinary issue-selection, not deception — every PAC leads with the voter's top concern.
effectiveness: won — reframes her strongest point ('voting with dollars') into evidence of a stealth campaign
confidence: medium — effective reframe but rests on Greenwald's unverified characterization of the ads (lines 1200-1232)

move: Refuse to 'list Biden's corruption' on demand; force the challenger to first agree/disagree with the itemized Trump facts
how_it_works: When pressed to balance the ledger, Greenwald inverts the burden: before any comparison, the challenger must engage the specific Trump/Kushner financial facts already laid out, denying the opponent a clean topic-switch to Biden.
evidence_quote: Do you agree or disagree with the claims that I've made about those? ... No, I know, but we're building a comparison. ... I'll leave it to the audience to decide if I've defended your claim.
counter: Greenwald's opponent's own line is the counter: 'you still have not addressed anything about Biden' — keep the proposition's COMPARATIVE structure front and center so refusing to weigh Biden reads as ducking half the claim.
effectiveness: neutral — Greenwald controls the exchange but the challenger lands the fair hit that a 'more corrupt THAN Biden' claim requires actually weighing Biden

move: Counterexample-strip the 'highly discriminate, no civilians' claim by forcing a concession on the school and bridge
how_it_works: Against the IRGC-only framing, he refuses the deflection ('misfiring intel') and isolates the bridge until the challenger admits 'I'm not going to get hung up on one bridge,' which concedes civilian targeting in principle.
evidence_quote: But what about that bridge? ... So the bridge was a bridge built to be used by civilians, right? ... I'm not going to get hung up on one bridge
counter: Don't concede the bridge as civilian — contest the single example's classification rather than waving it away, which reads as admission.
effectiveness: won — the 'no civilian infrastructure except one bridge' claim collapses the moment the bridge is conceded civilian

move: Expose the self-contradiction in 'Iranians are suicidal martyrs' vs 'they're now at the negotiating table'
how_it_works: He pins the irrationality claim against the observable fact of ongoing diplomacy: people who genuinely seek death would not be negotiating an end to the war — so the 'cosmic war' framing is internally inconsistent.
evidence_quote: If the Iranians are these extremely irrational people who seek martyrdom and want to die, why are we now negotiating an attempt to negotiate an end to this war? ... Why would they want the war to end then?
counter: The challenger's attempt ('because the end of the regime is coming if they can't get to the table') — reframe negotiation as coerced survival, not evidence of rationality, to dissolve the contradiction.
effectiveness: won — the contradiction lands; the rationality-vs-martyrdom framing visibly wobbles

move: The audience-capture 'have you ever thought about going and fighting in this war you're cheering on?'
how_it_works: Shifts the moral burden onto the pro-war young challenger personally: if the war is worth it, are you willing to risk your own life? It converts an abstract policy claim into a personal skin-in-the-game test the audience watches him fail to meet.
evidence_quote: You seem like a young guy to me. Have you ever thought about going and fighting in this war that you're cheering on? ... I mean, I've thought about joining the military before. I don't know about this war specifically.
counter: Reframe: 'advocacy doesn't require enlistment any more than voting for police requires becoming a cop' — sever the personal-participation hostage from the policy merits.
effectiveness: won — the hedged answer ('not this war specifically') undercuts the challenger's bravado on camera
confidence: high — lines 2204-2208, also the cold-open hook at lines 5-8

source_video.title_hint: David Wood CATCHES Muslim Apologist LYING

move: The footnote 'gotcha' — let the opponent cite a source as 'authentic,' then read the source's own footnote grading it 'weak'
how_it_works: Korah cites Ibn Kathir's al-Bidayah as 'authentically reported' that Gabriel comforted Muhammad. Wood pulls up the very page on screen, follows footnote 4 to its citation, and reads that the narration is graded weak — turning her cited authority into the instrument of her refutation.
evidence_quote: The report is weak. The report that Korah just said is authentic is actually weak. ... Either Korah just lied right there, or she has no clue what she's talking about.
counter: Cite the grade WITH the source ('reported in al-Bidayah, though Ibn Asakir grades the isnad weak') so the opponent can't spring the footnote; or contest whether a weak narration is still admissible corroboration.
effectiveness: won — the on-screen footnote read is decisive; the 'authentic' claim is publicly falsified

source_video.title_hint: David Wood CATCHES Muslim Apologist LYING

move: Pre-frame the audience with a forced binary ('she's either ignorant or she's lying') BEFORE revealing the evidence
how_it_works: He repeatedly primes viewers with a dichotomy and 'everyone check this out / follow the argument' callouts, so by the time the weak-grade footnote appears, the audience has already been steered into one of only two damning readings.
evidence_quote: she's either ignorant or she's lying she's either ignorant or she's lying but just i want everyone to follow the argument here ... let's find out
counter: Reject the false dilemma openly before he reveals the source: 'a third option is the narration is genuinely disputed among graders' — deny the pre-loaded binary so the reveal doesn't auto-confirm a verdict.
effectiveness: won — combined with E414 the priming makes the footnote reveal feel like a verdict rather than a data point
confidence: medium — clearly effective rhetoric, but 'won' rests on the unanswered framing; opponent's full rebuttal isn't in the clip
